- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early and then drops too sharply, missing subsequent mean-reversion or consolidation phases.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, particularly when true values show a downward trend.
- Forecast exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is below 75.
- Model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, overshooting downward corrections after upward spikes.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true values by 1–3 days in the middle of the 30-day window, especially during consolidation phases.
- When true values show a clear downward trend after a peak, model often fails to adjust downward in the 2nd half of the forecast.
- Model overfits recent high values, leading to overestimation of future prices when recent prices are already high.
